verses.text: Bless the LORD, my soul! LORD my God, you are so great. You wear honor and majesty like a robe.
You wrap yourself in light like a garment and stretch out the heavens like a curtain.
You set the beams of your rooms in the waters. You ride the clouds like a chariot and walk on the wings of the wind.
You make winds your messengers and flames of fire your servants.
You laid the earth on its foundations so it would never be moved.
You wrapped it in deep water like a cloak. The waters stood higher than the mountains.
At your rebuke they ran. At the sound of your thunder they rushed away.
The mountains rose and the valleys sank into the places you set for them.
You drew a line the waters can’t cross, so they’ll never come back to cover the earth.
You send springs into the valleys, and they run between the mountains.
Every animal in the fields drinks from them. Wild donkeys come and quench their thirst.
Birds nest beside the streams and sing from the branches.
From your rooms above, you water the mountains. The earth is filled with the fruit of what you do.
You grow grass for livestock and plants for people to tend, so they can bring food out of the ground:
wine to lift their hearts, oil to make their faces shine, and bread to give them strength.
The LORD’s trees drink their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
Birds build their nests there. The stork makes its home in the cypresses.
The high mountains are home to wild goats. The rocks shelter the rock badgers.
You set the moon to mark the seasons. The sun knows when it’s time to go down.
You bring on the dark, and night comes. Then all the forest animals come out and prowl.
Young lions roar for prey and look to God for their food.
When the sun comes up, they slip away and lie down in their dens.
Then people go out to work and keep at it until evening.
LORD, look how much you’ve made! You made it all with wisdom. The earth is full of your riches.
There’s the sea, huge and wide, full of creatures too many to count, from the smallest to the largest.
Ships sail there, and Leviathan is there too, the creature you made to play in the sea.
They all look to you to give them food when it’s time.
You give it, and they gather it up. You open your hand, and they have their fill of good things.
When you hide your face, they’re terrified. When you take their breath away, they die and go back to dust.
You send out your Spirit, and they come to life. You make the face of the earth new again.
May the LORD’s glory last forever. May the LORD take joy in what he’s made.
He looks at the earth and it shakes. He touches the mountains and they smoke.
I’ll sing to the LORD as long as I live. I’ll praise my God as long as I’m here.
May what I think about please him. I’ll take joy in the LORD.
Let sinners be swept off the earth. Let the wicked be gone. Bless the LORD, my soul. Praise the LORD!
